{"id": "44665cf1-4b85-4777-a73a-c717ca71e4ad", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_Kt2503TQJwxQzSLZ9V9LIW", "content": "[{'text': '# Review mode: Amazon EBS operational review\\n\\nReview mode answers \"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\". It is entirely read-only. Run each area per Region, rate each finding with the scale in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md), and write the report with [review-report-format.md](review-report-format.md).\\n\\nThe Capacity and quota headroom section is also a shared capability. Troubleshoot paths use it when an operation failed on a limit.\\n\\n## Capacity and quota headroom\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\nRun every check below even when the error looks simple. A user who reports a quota error has already failed to fix it alone, so give documented findings in the verdict format, not a short chat reply. Whether the run is a chat or a formal investigation is decided by how the user starts it, not by this skill.\\n\\n1. If an operation failed, quote the error and name the quota it refers to. For example \"You have exceeded your maximum io2 IOPS limit of 100000 IOPS in this region\" refers to the regional io2 IOPS quota, which is separate from the per-volume maximum.\\n2. `ListServiceQuotas --service-code ebs`: quota name, code, applied `Value`, `Adjustable`. Find quotas by name; never hardcode codes. `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota` shows the default.\\n3. Compute usage from the inventory:\\n   - Provisioned IOPS: sum of `Iops` for io1 volumes and for io2 volumes, separately.\\n   - Storage per type: sum of `Size` per volume type, converted from GiB to TiB.\\n   - Snapshots per Region: count of `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self`.\\n   - Fast snapshot restore: `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores` count of enabled entries.\\n4. `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` for pending requests. Never propose a duplicate.\\n\\n**Rating rule**\\n\\n- Usage at or above 80% of the applied quota is flagged. The 80% value is configurable; ask the operator if they use a different one.\\n- A quota that blocked an operation is `High`.\\n- A quota flagged at or above the threshold is `Medium`, or `High` if the user states a planned increase that would exceed it.\\n- Unreadable quota or usage is `Indeterminate`.\\n\\n**Fix**\\n\\n- Adjustable: a pre-filled Service Quotas request (service code `ebs`, quota code as read, desired value) proposed as a directed action. The desired value is the user\\'s stated need, or current usage plus the request that failed. No fixed multipliers.\\n- Not adjustable: draft the AWS Support case text (service, quota name, Region, desired value, business justification).\\n- Name the quotas that commonly cause problems: per-Region IOPS for io1 and io2, per-Region storage per volume type, snapshots per Region, and fast snapshot restore.\\n\\n## Observability\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EBS namespace: alarms on `VolumeQueueLength`, latency (`VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency`, or `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeTotalWriteTime` math), throughput, and `BurstBalance` for gp2, st1 and sc1.\\n2. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EC2 namespace: `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` on instances that publish them.\\n3. Which volumes are critical: ask the operator, or use tags they name. Do not infer criticality from tag values by yourself.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a critical volume with no Amazon EBS alarm is `Medium`. `High` if the operator says the volume backs a production database or service. An alarm in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` for a long time is `Low` (it may be on a deleted volume).\\n\\n**Fix**: propose alarms with metric, dimensions (`VolumeAvg*` need `VolumeId` and `InstanceId`) and the threshold the operator chooses.\\n\\n## Cost hygiene\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. gp2 volumes: gp3 candidates. gp3 has 20% lower price per GiB than gp2 and includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s.\\n2. Unattached volumes: `DescribeVolumes` with `status=available`.\\n3. Over-provisioned IOPS or throughput: measured vs provisioned, and provisioned above the instance EBS baseline (see [troubleshoot-billing.md](troubleshoot-billing.md) step 6).\\n4. AWS Compute Optimizer `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` if enabled (optional).\\n\\n**Rating rule**: `Low` by default. `Medium` when the operator names cost as a goal or the resource is large relative to the account\\'s Amazon EBS spend as shown in Cost Explorer.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyVolume` to gp3 with IOPS and throughput sized as in [troubleshoot-volume-modification.md](troubleshoot-volume-modification.md) step 6; snapshot then delete for unattached volumes. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Resilience\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. Inventory volumes (`DescribeVolumes`), including root volumes.\\n2. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: `GetLifecyclePolicies` (state `ENABLED`) and `GetLifecyclePolicy` for target tags and resource type. Target tags are case sensitive. Note default policies, which target the Region\\'s volumes or instances without recent backups.\\n3. AWS Backup: `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection` (selection by resource ARN, by tag condition, or all resources of a type), and `ListProtectedResources`.\\n4. Match each volume to a policy or a selection. A volume that matches none is unprotected.\\n5. For protected volumes, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true for the latest recovery point, and the latest `aws:dlm:*` tagged snapshot of the volume. Compare its age with the policy schedule. Without that parameter, the call also returns manual snapshots, which are not backups from the plan.\\n6. Cross-Region copy for disaster recovery: copy actions in DLM policies or AWS Backup copy rules.\\n7. Ask the operator for their recovery point objective. Do not assume one.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: an unprotected volume the operator calls critical is `High`. A protected volume whose latest recovery point is older than its own schedule is `High` (the backup may be failing). No cross-Region copy where the operator needs Regional disaster recovery is `Medium`. Unprotected non-critical volumes are `Low`.\\n\\n**Fix**: tag the volume to match an existing policy, add it to a backup selection, or create a policy. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Encryption posture\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault` and `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId` per Region.\\n2. Unencrypted volumes and snapshots (`Encrypted` is false).\\n3. For keys in use, AWS KMS `DescribeKey` state. A disabled or pending-deletion key in use is a risk.\\n4. Snapshot exposure: `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState` per Region, and `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self --restorable-by-user-ids all` for snapshots that are public now.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a key in use that is disabled or pending deletion is `High`. A public snapshot is `High`. Encryption by default off is `Medium`. Unencrypted volumes are `Medium`, or `High` if the operator says the data is regulated. Snapshot block public access in the `unblocked` state is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: turn on encryption by default; re-encrypt with the steps in [troubleshoot-encryption.md](troubleshoot-encryption.md); turn on snapshot block public access (`block-all-sharing`, or `block-new-sharing` while existing public shares are reviewed). All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Deletion protection\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeInstanceAttribute --attribute blockDeviceMapping` for `DeleteOnTermination` on each attached volume. A data volume with `DeleteOnTermination` true is deleted when the instance terminates.\\n2. Recycle Bin `ListRules` for `EBS_SNAPSHOT` (and for AMIs if the account uses them).\\n3. Snapshot lock: `DescribeLockedSnapshots` for snapshots the operator must keep.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a critical data volume with `DeleteOnTermination` true is `High`. No Recycle Bin rule for snapshots is `Medium`. No lock on snapshots the operator says are compliance records is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyInstanceAttribute` to set `DeleteOnTermination` false on the data volume, a Recycle Bin retention rule, or a snapshot lock. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- Review mode is entirely read-only. It never runs a mutating call.\\n- Every fix is listed under \"Proposed actions\" in the report with exact parameters, expected effect, cost direction and rollback. Each one needs a directed action approved on the approval card.\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon EBS quotas: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/ebs-service.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-resource-quotas.html\\n- Requesting a quota increase: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/latest/userguide/request-quota-increase.html\\n- Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon EBS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/using_cloudwatch_ebs.html\\n- gp3 and gp2: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html\\n- Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-lifecycle.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-ami-policy.html\\n- AWS Backup resource assignment: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/assigning-resources.html\\n- Encryption by default: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/encryption-by-default.html\\n- Block public access for snapshots: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/block-public-access-snapshots.html\\n- AWS Backup ListRecoveryPointsByResource: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/APIReference/API_ListRecoveryPointsByResource.html\\n- DeleteOnTermination: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/terminating-instances.html\\n- Recycle Bin: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/recycle-bin.html\\n- Snapshot lock: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-snapshot-lock.html\\n- Fast snapshot restore: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-fast-snapshot-restore.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_oAYkhmziHC9jdelqv9HKe5", "content": "[{'text': '# Data collection: read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks\\n\\nLoad this file on every request. Every value in a verdict or a review comes from one of these calls. | Snapshots per Region (L-309BACF6) | 100,000 | 9 | 0.009% |
| Fast snapshot restore (L-631ECBD3) | 5 | 0 enabled | 0% |

- `describe_fast_snapshot_restores` returned an empty list.
- `list_requested_service_quota_change_history` for `ebs` returned no requests, so none are pending.
- All the quotas above are adjustable.

**Instance EBS limits versus attached provisioned volumes.** Conversions use MB/s × 1,000,000 / 1,048,576. Both running instances are exposed to the issue below. The rest are stopped, so it matters only when they start.

- **i-0123456789abcdef0_2 (t3.medium, running). High.**
  - Instance limits: baseline 2000 IOPS / 41.4 MiB/s, maximum 11,800 IOPS / 248.5 MiB/s.
  - **vol-0123456789abcdef0_5 (io2) is provisioned at 20,000 IOPS, which exceeds the instance maximum of 11,800, so the excess cannot be delivered.**
  - Sum of attached provisioned IOPS is 23,000 (gp3 root 3,000 plus io2 20,000), against a 2,000 baseline and an 11,800 maximum.
  - Provisioned gp3 throughput is 125 MiB/s, which is above the 41.4 MiB/s baseline but below the maximum.
- **i-0123456789abcdef0_4 (t3.micro, stopped). High.**
  - Instance limits: baseline 500 IOPS / 10.4 MiB/s, maximum 11,800 IOPS / 248.5 MiB/s.
  - **vol-0123456789abcdef0_24 (gp3) is provisioned at 16,000 IOPS, above the 11,800 maximum.** Its CloudWatch peak was 11,807 IOPS, which matches the instance cap.
  - Sum is 19,000 IOPS (root 3,000 plus 16,000). Throughput sum is 250 MiB/s, just above the 248.5 MiB/s maximum.
- **i-0123456789abcdef0_3 (c6i.xlarge, stopped). Medium.**
  - Instance limits: baseline 6000 IOPS / 149.0 MiB/s, maximum 40,000 IOPS / 1192.1 MiB/s.
  - The IOPS sum is 16,000: 3,000 + 1,000 (io2) + 3,000 + 3,000 + 6,000. That is above the baseline and below the maximum.
  - The gp3 throughput sum is 625 MiB/s (125 + 125 + 125 + 250), above the baseline and below the maximum.
  - The 250 MiB/s volume vol-0123456789abcdef0_7 (and the unattached vol-0123456789abcdef0_8) is individually above the 149.0 MiB/s baseline. So the sum can only be sustained within the burst maximum.
- **i-0123456789abcdef0_6 (t3.micro, stopped). Low.** Sum is 3,100 IOPS (root gp2 100 plus gp3 3,000), above the 500 baseline and below the 11,800 maximum. gp3 throughput of 125 MiB/s is above the 10.4 MiB/s baseline and below the maximum.
- **i-0123456789abcdef0_7 (m5.large) and i-0123456789abcdef0_9 (m5.xlarge).** Their gp2 volumes are well below the instance limits.
- **t2.micro instances (i-0123456789abcdef0_10, i-0123456789abcdef0_5, i-0123456789abcdef0_11).** t2.micro has no EBS-optimized info (`unsupported`), so no limit comparison is possible. **Indeterminate.**

### 3. Encryption posture

**Severity: High. This is unencrypted data at rest.**

- `get_ebs_encryption_by_default` returned **false**, and the default KMS key is `alias/aws/ebs`.
- All 24 of 24 volumes and all 9 of 9 snapshots are unencrypted. Every volume and snapshot listed in the inventory above is affected.
- No customer KMS key is in use by any volume or snapshot, so `kms describe_key` had nothing to check.
- `get_snapshot_block_public_access_state` returned `unblocked` (ManagedBy=account). Severity: Low to Medium, because public sharing is not blocked.
- `describe_snapshots` with RestorableByUserIds=['all'] returned an empty list, so there are no public snapshots. Both AMIs report Public=false.

### 4. Deletion protection

- **No non-root (data) volume has DeleteOnTermination=true.**
  - All 7 data volumes have DOT=false: vol-0123456789abcdef0_9, vol-0123456789abcdef0_10, vol-0123456789abcdef0_5, vol-0123456789abcdef0_23, vol-0123456789abcdef0_18, vol-0123456789abcdef0_2, vol-0123456789abcdef0.
  - The same applies to vol-0123456789abcdef0_7 and vol-0123456789abcdef0_24.
  - All 9 root volumes have DOT=true.
  - Severity: Low. The consequence of DOT=false is that data volumes outlive their instances, which is orphan-cost risk rather than data-loss risk.
- `describe_locked_snapshots` returned an empty list, so no snapshots are locked. Severity: Medium for the 9 snapshots, which have no lock.
- Recycle Bin retention rules **could not be checked**, so protection against accidental snapshot or AMI deletion is **Indeterminate** (see Gaps).
- There is limited snapshot backup coverage. Only 2 of 24 volumes have a self-owned snapshot. I did not query DLM policies, so whether another backup mechanism exists is Indeterminate.

### 5. Cost hygiene

**Severity: Medium.**

- **gp2 volumes (gp3 candidates), 7:** vol-0123456789abcdef0_10, vol-0123456789abcdef0_21, vol-0123456789abcdef0_11, vol-0123456789abcdef0_13, vol-0123456789abcdef0_14, vol-0123456789abcdef0_19 and vol-0123456789abcdef0_15. Together they are 64 GiB. Severity: Low to Medium.
- **Unattached volumes, 6, 287 GiB.**
  - vol-0123456789abcdef0_8 (gp3 200 GiB, 6000 IOPS / 250 MiB/s) and vol-0123456789abcdef0_12 (gp3 50 GiB, 6000 IOPS) carry provisioned performance above the gp3 baseline while attached to nothing.
  - vol-0123456789abcdef0_4 (gp3 25 GiB, 3500 IOPS / 130 MiB/s) has been unattached since creation on 2023-11-13, and is tagged auto-delete=no.
  - The other three are small: vol-0123456789abcdef0_15 (10 GiB gp2), vol-0123456789abcdef0_3 (1 GiB) and vol-0123456789abcdef0_22 (1 GiB).
- **Provisioned versus observed over 14 days** (CloudWatch peaks at 5-minute resolution; the stats below are computed from VolumeReadOps/WriteOps and VolumeReadBytes/WriteBytes):
  - **vol-0123456789abcdef0_5 (io2, 20,000 IOPS): peak 0.35 IOPS and 0.007 MiB/s across 4,034 datapoints (14 days).** It is idle and heavily over-provisioned. **High** cost finding, and the instance cannot deliver that IOPS anyway.
  - vol-0123456789abcdef0_24 (gp3, 16,000 IOPS): peak 11,807 IOPS and 46.1 MiB/s over 43 datapoints. It uses the instance cap rather than the provisioned figure. 13,000 IOPS are paid above the 3,000 baseline.
  - vol-0123456789abcdef0_7 (gp3, 6000 IOPS / 250 MiB/s): peak 500 IOPS and 125.1 MiB/s over 43 datapoints. Provisioned IOPS are not used.
  - vol-0123456789abcdef0_18 (io2, 1000 IOPS): peak 1000.01 IOPS over 43 datapoints, so it is at its provisioned limit.
  - vol-0123456789abcdef0_12 (unattached): no datapoints.

## (c) Gaps

1. **`rbin list_rules` with ResourceType=EBS_SNAPSHOT failed.** The call was cancelled before execution (ELEVATED_ACTIONS_DISABLED). Recycle Bin retention for snapshots is therefore **Indeterminate**.
2. **`rbin list_rules` with ResourceType=EC2_IMAGE failed** with the same error, so Recycle Bin retention for AMIs is **Indeterminate**.
3. `kms describe_key` was not run, because no volume or snapshot references a customer KMS key. The default `alias/aws/ebs` is an AWS-managed key and I did not describe it.
4. Several metric windows are short.
   - Metrics for the volumes created on 2026-11-11 cover only about 19 hours, and CloudWatch emits EBS metrics only when there is I/O.
   - The io2 volume vol-0123456789abcdef0_5 has 14 days of data. It is attached to the running instance.
   - Only 6 volumes were sampled, so the findings above do not cover the other 18.
5. DLM lifecycle policies, AWS Backup, instance-level EBS metrics and volume-modification history were not queried, because they were not requested.
6. t2.micro has no EBS limit data, so the per-instance comparison could not be made for i-0123456789abcdef0_10, i-0123456789abcdef0_5 and i-0123456789abcdef0_11.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

Use use_aws with ONLY read-only calls (describe/get/list). Do not mutate anything. Report concise structured findings with real IDs and values from the APIs; never invent anything. List every API that failed/was denied/gated as a Gap (do not try to bypass an approval gate).

Cover:

1. VOLUME LIST (for matching): ec2 describe_volumes (id, type, size, state, attached instance, Name tag, tags) in us-east-1.

2. OBSERVABILITY: cloudwatch describe_alarms (paginate) - identify alarms in namespace AWS/EBS (VolumeQueueLength, VolumeAvgReadLatency/VolumeAvgWriteLatency or VolumeTotalReadTime/WriteTime math, throughput, BurstBalance for gp2/st1/sc1, VolumeThroughputPercentage) and AWS/EC2 (EBSIOBalance%, EBSByteBalance%). Alarms may use metric math (Metrics field), so check those too. Map which volumes/instances have alarms and which have none. Flag any alarm in INSUFFICIENT_DATA (and whether its VolumeId still exists), and any alarm currently in ALARM. Check alarm actions (do they notify anything?).

3. RESILIENCE: 
 - Data Lifecycle Manager: dlm get_lifecycle_policies, then get_lifecycle_policy for each (state ENABLED? target tags, resource type, schedule, retention, cross-region copy actions). Target tags are case sensitive.
 - AWS Backup: backup list_backup_plans, list_backup_selections, get_backup_selection (by ARN, tag condition, or resource type), list_protected_resources, and for protected EBS volumes list_recovery_points_by_resource with ManagedByAWSBackupOnly=True to find the latest recovery point; also check copy rules (cross-region) in plans via get_backup_plan.
 - Match each volume to a DLM policy or Backup selection; list unprotected volumes. For protected volumes compare the latest recovery point / latest aws:dlm:* snapshot age with the schedule (flag stale = older than own schedule). Use ec2 describe_snapshots OwnerIds=['self'] filtered by volume-id for latest snapshot start time per volume if needed.
 - Cross-region copy present? 
 - Do NOT assume an RPO.

4. Check AWS Health for open events affecting EBS/EC2 in us-east-1 (health describe_events, region us-east-1 / the health endpoint) and ec2 describe_volume_status for any impaired volumes (filter volume-status.status=impaired or just report non-ok). Also check fis list_experiments for any running experiments.

Return: (a) the alarm coverage table (volume/instance -> alarms), (b) resilience coverage table per volume (policy/plan, latest recovery point time, schedule, stale?), (c) findings per area with severity suggestion (High/Medium/Low/Indeterminate) and evidence, (d) Gaps.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
